title: NAV, valuation, expenses and loads
objectives: Explain the expense ratio, loads and trail commission.
body_md:
## NAV

**NAV per unit = (Market value of assets − liabilities and expenses) ÷ number of units outstanding**

NAV is computed **daily** after market close and published by the AMC and AMFI.

## Valuation

- Listed equity at the closing price on the exchange.
- Debt securities valued using prices from **AMFI-approved valuation agencies**.

## Costs

| Cost | Notes |
|---|---|
| **Total Expense Ratio (TER)** | Charged daily within the NAV; covers management fee, RTA, audit, distribution; slab-based, falling as the fund grows |
| **Exit load** | Charged on redemption within a stated period; credited to the scheme |
| **Entry load** | Abolished in 2009 |
| **STT / stamp duty / GST** | Statutory charges |

## Direct vs Regular

The **Direct plan** has a lower TER because there is no distributor commission. The **Regular plan** pays a **trail commission** to the distributor, which is built into the TER.

## Example

Assets ₹1,010 crore, liabilities ₹10 crore, units 100 crore: **NAV = ₹10.00**.

> **Exam tip:** Compute NAV by hand once; the formula often appears.
example: Assets ₹520 crore, liabilities ₹20 crore, units 25 crore. NAV = (520 − 20) ÷ 25 = ₹20.
say: The expense ratio is already inside the NAV; you will not see a separate bill.
Direct plans cost less; regular plans include our service and trail commission.
never: There is no cost, the fund is free.
Entry load of 2.25% applies on all funds.
